cleaning.why: 0 K is a sensor error, not weather.
More than 100 mm in one hour is a sensor error.
Fewer than 100 vehicles in an hour: the road was closed or the counter was down.
The source marks a holiday only on its midnight row; every hour of that day is a holiday.
A holiday whose midnight hour is missing from the data was never marked; the calendar names it.
Hours with several weather rows repeat the same volume; keep one row, with the most severe weather.
Named days on which traffic stays near normal (Columbus Day, Veterans Day and others) are ordinary days for the model; only the quiet holidays listed in the configuration count.

candidates.notes: Gradient boosting in scikit-learn; strong and fast.
Averages many trees; robust but large and slower to score.
Gradient boosting in LightGBM; usually strongest on tabular data. Explained with SHAP.
Small neural network on scaled inputs and a scaled target; hardest to interpret.
One readable regression tree; unstable and prone to overfitting.
The same lookup table with quiet holidays as an eighth day type.
Ridge on squares and pairwise products of the numbers: curved effects and interactions.
Ordinary least squares; each coefficient is directly readable.
Linear with L2 shrinkage; stable when features are correlated.
Mean of the same hour and weekday in training. The bar to beat.
Linear with L1 shrinkage; drops weak features.

champion.rule: lowest validation RMSE; models within 5.0 vehicles/hour count as equal and the simplest of them wins (fewest input variables, then smallest file)

verdict.text: Validation error is 6% below training error: no overfitting. If anything the training years are the harder ones to fit; the table of training error by year shows which. On the complexity curve the validation error is lowest at max_leaf_nodes = 16 (345) and the chosen setting (10) is within 2% of it: more capacity would not help, so the model is not underfitting either.
